summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Distributed Sharded Transactions; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [low] Regardless of the write concern specified for the transaction, the commit operation for a sharded cluster transaction includes some parts that use {w: "majority"}. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-sharded-clusters.md

[low] A number of issues with sharded multi-document transactions in clusters of 2 or more shards have been identified that result in returning incorrect results and missing reads and writes. Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-server-for-mongodb/7.0/release_notes/7.0.8-5.html

[low] The issues with sharded multi-document transactions occur when the transactions’ metadata is being concurrently modified by using moveChunk, moveRange, movePrimary, renameCollection, drop, and reshardCollection operations. Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-server-for-mongodb/7.0/release_notes/7.0.8-5.html

[low] If a multi-shard transaction interacts with an operation that takes the critical section on multiple shards, the interaction can result in a distributed deadlock. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

[low] SERVER-86583 fixed the issue with reads returning incomplete results and mismatched sharding metadata when performed on sharded collections with the readConcern: snapshot and an atClusterTime values. Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-server-for-mongodb/7.0/release_notes/7.0.8-5.html

[high] You cannot run transactions on a sharded cluster that has a shard with writeConcernMajorityJournalDefault set to false. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-sharded-clusters.md, https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern

[high] Transactions whose write operations span multiple shards will error and abort if any transaction operation reads from or writes to a shard that contains an arbiter. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-sharded-clusters.md, https://severalnines.com/blog/transaction-considerations-mongodb-production/

[medium] Distributed transactions in MongoDB were developed incrementally across three versions: single-node transactions in v3.2, single replica set transactions in v4.0, and full sharded cluster transactions in v4.2. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/formal-methods-beyond-correctness-isolation-permissiveness-distributed-transactions, https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-transactions-and-read--write-concerns

[low] MongoDB has supported distributed, multi-document transactions since 2019, enabling ACID, cross-shard transactions at snapshot isolation. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/formal-methods-beyond-correctness-isolation-permissiveness-distributed-transactions

[high] MongoDB 4.2 added distributed transactions for operations across multiple collections and shards, maintaining identical syntax to version 4.0 transactions. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern, https://severalnines.com/blog/transaction-considerations-mongodb-production/

[low] The minimum feature compatibility version for using transactions with a replica set is MongoDB 4.0, whereas for a sharded cluster it is 4.2. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://severalnines.com/blog/transaction-considerations-mongodb-production/

[high] For transactions on a sharded cluster, only the snapshot read concern provides a consistent snapshot across multiple shards. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-sharded-clusters.md, https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-transactions-and-read--write-concerns

[low] The issues with sharded multi-document transactions are fully fixed in MongoDB 4.4.29, 5.0.25, 6.0.14, 7.0.8, and are included in Percona Server for MongoDB 4.4.29-28, 5.0.26-22, 6.0.14-11 and 7.0.8-5. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-server-for-mongodb/7.0/release_notes/7.0.8-5.html

[low] If you are using sharded multi-document transactions or queryable encryption, upgrade to Percona Server for MongoDB 7.0.8-5 as soon as possible. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-server-for-mongodb/7.0/release_notes/7.0.8-5.html

[low] Transactions that affect multiple shards incur a greater performance cost as operations are coordinated across multiple participating nodes over the network. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-transactions-and-read--write-concerns
